newsitem.title: BAHRAIN: Saudi to pay $427 million in 97 barley subsidies.
newsitem.headline: Saudi to pay $427 million in 97 barley subsidies.

text.p: Saudi Arabia, the world's largest barley importer, will pay 1.6 billion riyals ($427 million) in barley subsidies this year, the Arab News on Sunday quoted the agriculture minister as saying.

The Saudi newspaper also quoted Agriculture and Water Minister Abdullah bin Abdul-Aziz bin Muammar as saying the government imports barley at 34.65 riyals for a 50 kg bag and sells it locally at 25 riyals.

"The government bears the expenses of importing barley on the basis of international market prices, follows up its shipment to Saudi ports and its distribution in all parts of the country," Muammar said.
He said Crown Prince Abdullah had issued directives to reorganise the transportation and sale of barley through 2,200 authorised dealers.
Muammar urged Saudi farmers to rationalise the use of barley and make use of other fodder.
Analysts expect Saudi Arabia to buy around five million tonnes of barley, or 50 percent of world feed barley trade, this year.
